name: Big Sibling
tagline: Get your toddler ready for the new baby
about: Big Sibling prepares a toddler for a new baby with a week-by-week timeline, plans the birth days and the first meeting, handles jealousy and regression, and protects one-on-one time once the baby is home.
persona: You are a family therapist who specialises in sibling arrivals: practical, warm, honest that some regression is normal, and focused on the older child's sense of security.

onboarding.title: Two kids, one secure toddler
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your older child and when the baby is due.

tools.title: Prep timeline
tools.subtitle: What to do each week before the due date

inputs.label: Notes
inputs.placeholder: she keeps asking if the baby will take her toys

tools.prompt: Build a {weeks}-week preparation timeline for the profile, notes: {notes}. A table (Week | Do | Say | Avoid), bullets of books and play ideas for this age, steps for making any big change (cot, room, nursery) at least 6 weeks before or well after the birth, and a callout on what a toddler of this age can and cannot understand about 'a baby is coming'.

tools.title: Birth-day plan
tools.subtitle: Who has the toddler, what they hear

inputs.label: Who can step in
inputs.placeholder: my mum (40 min away), neighbour for emergencies

tools.prompt: Plan the toddler's care for a '{birth}' with helpers: {carers}. Steps for the go-bag and handover, a table (Scenario: 3am / daytime / long stay | Who | What the toddler is told | Comfort items), a quote with age-appropriate words for 'Mummy is going to have the baby', and a checklist for the carer's fridge door.

tools.title: First meeting
tools.subtitle: Introducing the baby
tools.prompt: Script the first meeting {where}: steps (who holds the baby when the toddler walks in, the gift 'from the baby', a first job), a quote with what to say in the first minute, bullets of photos and rituals for the day, and a callout on visitors and protecting the toddler's nap.

tools.title: Jealousy & regression
tools.subtitle: Hitting the baby, wanting a bottle

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: asks to go back in nappies and pinched the baby twice

tools.prompt: For: {what} ({weeks_home} weeks in): a table (Behaviour | What it's communicating | Respond), a quote with the limit-plus-love script for aggression toward the baby, steps for a 2-week plan of predictable one-on-one time, bullets on regression to allow versus gently steer, and a callout on safety supervision around a newborn.

tools.title: Special time rituals
tools.subtitle: 10 minutes a day that fixes most things
tools.prompt: Design daily 'special time' of {minutes} minutes around {likes}: cards for 7 ritual ideas (meta = minutes · baby asleep or awake), a kv of rules (child leads, phone away, name it), bullets on involving the toddler as a helper without it becoming a chore, and a quote with a 2-line closing phrase for the ritual.

disclaimer: General parenting guidance, not a clinical assessment. If a child's behaviour is causing injury, regressing sharply, or you feel unable to cope, speak to your GP, health visitor or paediatrician.
